newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen hot this weekend, cooler Monday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen hot this weekend, cooler Monday.

text.p: A heat wave was expected to hit the U.S. Midwest this weekend, with temperatures above 90 degrees Fahrenheit, but meteorologists said a cold front would move in by Monday, bringing temperatures back to normal.
"The readings will be into the middle to upper 90s in the west today," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.

"Des Moines and Peoria should be above 95 degrees on Saturday. Sunday and Monday we will have a front moving southward into the Midwest. We're talking about rainfall of 0.25 to 1.00 inch with 40 to 60 percent coverage," he said.
But Freese-Notis meteorolgist Craig Solberg said rainfall may be lighter south of Interstate 80. That area received some rainfall last weekend and early this week but needs more moisture.
"The next couple of days for at least the western and southern Corn Belt will be the hottest weather of the summer so far," Solberg said. "We're becoming less optimistic about the rainfall."
He forecast 0.25 to 0.75 inch with 50 to 60 percent coverage by Monday. North of Interstate 80, the coverage should be closer to 70 percent, he said.
Forecasters agreed temperatures should return to normal next week, with readings in the mid- to upper-80s F.

"The heat should end on Sunday," Solberg said. "It looks like a nice cool down for next week with temperatures near normal. Precipitation next week will average a little bit below normal for the Corn Belt."
WSC's Burgio said long-range forecasts suggested temperatures would warm again next Thursday and Friday with a chance for showers on Saturday and Sunday.
